description:
​APEX TECH is a multidisciplinary team from Hanoi, uniting passionate technologists, data enthusiasts, and creative storytellers. Taking on the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, we aim to bring NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars back into the spotlight—transforming silent hardware relics into compelling, interactive human stories.

Core Strengths:

​- Tech-Driven Storytelling

​- Data, Research Synthesis

​- Agile Execution
summary:
ABANDONED, NOT FORGOTTEN is an interactive, bilingual (English/Vietnamese) web app built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript that turns NASA mission archives into an engaging "Space Archaeology" experience for students aged 10–15.

Addressing the Moon & Mars challenge, our platform reframes hardware left on lunar and Martian surfaces—Apollo 12 ALSEP, Mars Pathfinder, and Opportunity—as enduring scientific heritage. Learners explore 3-layer evidence dossiers (The Artifact, Why It Stayed, What Remains), track progress (3/3 artifacts), and earn a personalized Space Archaeologist Certificate.
details:
ABANDONED, NOT FORGOTTEN is an interactive, bilingual (English/Vietnamese) web application that turns official NASA mission archives into an engaging "Space Archaeology" investigation for students aged 10–15 and classroom learning.

How It Works & Creativity: Instead of presenting dense technical logs, our platform guides learners through three historic missions—Apollo 12 ALSEP, Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner, and the Opportunity rover—using a 3-layer evidence discovery model (The Artifact, Why It Stayed, and What Remains). Browser local storage tracks exploration progress (3/3 artifacts) and unlocks a personalized Space Archaeologist Certificate upon completion.

Impact & Benefits: By reframing hardware left on the Moon and Mars from "abandoned equipment" into enduring scientific heritage, the project makes lunar seismology, Mars geology, and planetary robotics accessible to non-English speaking students.

Tools, Data & Design Factors: Built with lightweight HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript, original vector illustrations, and hosted on Netlify, the app is fast, responsive, and offline-capable. All scientific facts were curated and verified directly from NASA PDS (Geosciences & Imaging Nodes) and NASA/JPL Photojournal (PIA19048) records.
